newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money high, central bank offers repo.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money high, central bank offers repo.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 18.0/19.0 percent from 16.0/17.0 percent on Wednesday morning.
Dealers said liquidity supply was tighter, with pressure boosted by the month-end factor. The central bank supplied 856 billion rupiah on Wednesday into the market.
"The market is already tight after the central bank scrapped the purchase of short-term securities (SBPUs) in the past few days," one local bank dealer said.
"Fears of possible tightening on Thursday due to the month-end factor seem to have worried operators," she said.
The central bank had tightened liquidity by raising short-term interest rates and cancelling the SBPU auction to reduce speculative dollar buying.
The bank, anticipating a liquidity squeeze at month-end, offered repo on central bank certificates (SBIs) for Wednesday.
Bank Indonesia offered repo on one-week SBIs at 13.75 percent while keeping short-term rates relatively expensive.

The bank offered one-to-two day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, five-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Dealers said longer-term money was also expensive following an increase in short-term rates. One-week and one-month money were at 17.00/17.25 and 16.75/17.00 percent, respectively.
They said arbitrage was still possible between the swap and the money markets due to interest differentials. Overnight swap was at par/0.05 points.
Overnight dollars remained expensive at 13.0 percent.

Dealers said the condition would continue for a few more days because the "anomalies", expensive short-term rupiah and dollars coupled with cheap swaps, were technical following last week's turmoil in the foreign exchange market.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 17.47 percent, compared with 16.58 percent on Monday.
